🐝 \u003cstrong\u003eSwarm workers now pull market data through the loader layer\u003c/strong\u003e: An investment-committee run on NVDA exposed a chain of gaps — workers wrote ad-hoc yfinance scripts, trusted a malformed latest bar (volume present, OHLC empty), leaked \u003ccode\u003eNaN\u003c/code\u003e into non-strict JSON, and a context-free continuation prompt re-routed to the wrong preset (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/198\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/198/hovercard\"\u003e#198\u003c/a\u003e, thanks @BillDin for an exceptional diagnosis plus both fixes). Swarm workers now get a local \u003ccode\u003eget_market_data\u003c/code\u003e tool backed by the same normalized loader registry as MCP — strict JSON, non-finite floats serialize as \u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e — wired into \u003cstrong\u003eevery market-data preset\u003c/strong\u003e (21 workers across 13 presets) with a prompt policy that steers OHLCV work tool-first (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/199\" data-hovercard-type=\"pull_request\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/199/hovercard\"\u003e#199\u003c/a\u003e); \u003ccode\u003erun_swarm\u003c/code\u003e takes an explicit \u003ccode\u003epreset_name\u003c/code\u003e and refuses ambiguous continuation fragments instead of silently falling back to \u003ccode\u003eequity_research_team\u003c/code\u003e (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/200\" data-hovercard-type=\"pull_request\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/200/hovercard\"\u003e#200\u003c/a\u003e). Grounding got smarter too: a bare US ticker like \u003ccode\u003eNVDA\u003c/code\u003e in a swarm prompt is promoted to \u003ccode\u003eNVDA.US\u003c/code\u003e (stopword-guarded), so workers start from authoritative pre-fetched prices. The tool joins the main agent registry as well — \u003cstrong\u003e48 tools\u003c/strong\u003e now. Also: \u003cstrong\u003eyour Docker data now survives updates\u003c/strong\u003e — persistent memory, the session search index, user-created skills, shadow accounts and broker config live in named volumes, so \u003ccode\u003edocker compose up --build\u003c/code\u003e no longer wipes them (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/197\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/197/hovercard\"\u003e#197\u003c/a\u003e, thanks @FlyerJ).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2026-06-10\u003c/strong\u003e 🐳 \u003cstrong\u003eDocker reaches a host-side Ollama out of the box\u003c/strong\u003e: Inside the container \u003ccode\u003elocalhost\u003c/code\u003e is the container itself, so the shipped \u003ccode\u003eOLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434\u003c/code\u003e failed the LLM preflight for every Dockerized Ollama setup. \u003ccode\u003edocker-compose.yml\u003c/code\u003e now defaults to \u003ccode\u003ehttp://host.docker.internal:11434\u003c/code\u003e (export \u003ccode\u003eOLLAMA_BASE_URL\u003c/code\u003e to point elsewhere) and adds the \u003ccode\u003ehost-gateway\u003c/code\u003e \u003ccode\u003eextra_hosts\u003c/code\u003e mapping so the same file works on Linux as well as Docker Desktop (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/196\" data-hovercard-type=\"pull_request\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/196/hovercard\"\u003e#196\u003c/a\u003e, thanks @ShahNewazKhan).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2026-06-09\u003c/strong\u003e 🔑 \u003cstrong\u003eClearer error when the Web UI is opened from another machine\u003c/strong\u003e: Reaching the chat from a non-loopback client (another machine, a VM host, a phone on your LAN) without \u003ccode\u003eAPI_AUTH_KEY\u003c/code\u003e set returned \u003ccode\u003e403\u003c/code\u003e on every sensitive endpoint — sending a message, listing sessions, live status — but the chat only showed a generic \"Failed to send message, please retry.\" The send path now surfaces the real reason — \u003cem\u003e\"Remote API access requires an API key. Add it in Settings, or run the backend on localhost for local-only use.\"\u003c/em\u003e — and the README's web-UI setup spells out the localhost-vs-LAN rule plus the three fixes (browse via \u003ccode\u003elocalhost\u003c/code\u003e on the same machine; set \u003ccode\u003eAPI_AUTH_KEY\u003c/code\u003e and enter it once in Settings; or \u003ccode\u003eVIBE_TRADING_TRUST_DOCKER_LOOPBACK=1\u003c/code\u003e for Docker Desktop's host gateway) (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/191\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/191/hovercard\"\u003e#191\u003c/a\u003e, thanks @mafia23).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdetails\u003e\n\u003csummary\u003eEarlier news\u003c/summary\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2026-06-08\u003c/strong\u003e 🔧 \u003cstrong\u003eGemini 3.x multi-turn tool-calling fix\u003c/strong\u003e: This completes the Gemini 3.x thinking-model fix. The 6/05 round-trip (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/176\" data-hovercard-type=\"pull_request\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/176/hovercard\"\u003e#176\u003c/a\u003e) only covered in-memory history, but the real agent loop replays history as OpenAI-format dicts where LangChain dropped the per-tool-call \u003ccode\u003ethought_signature\u003c/code\u003e before the request was built — so multi-turn tool calling still 400'd with \u003ccode\u003emissing thought_signature\u003c/code\u003e. It is now re-attached at the single \u003ccode\u003e_convert_input\u003c/code\u003e chokepoint both \u003ccode\u003einvoke\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003estream\u003c/code\u003e pass through (parallel calls, where only the first of N is signed, included) (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/184\" data-hovercard-type=\"pull_request\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/184/hovercard\"\u003e#184\u003c/a\u003e, thanks @ngoanpv).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2026-06-07\u003c/strong\u003e 🐝 \u003cstrong\u003eLive swarm status in the chat timeline\u003c/strong\u003e: When the agent launches a multi-agent swarm (investment committee, quant desk, risk committee, …), the chat now renders an inline \u003cstrong\u003estatus card\u003c/strong\u003e that streams each worker's state — waiting / running / done / failed / blocked / retrying — in real time, the same per-agent visibility the standalone swarm dashboard already had. Runtime events are bridged into the session SSE stream without changing the existing \u003ccode\u003e/swarm/runs\u003c/code\u003e API, and a finished card rehydrates from the final \u003ccode\u003erun_swarm\u003c/code\u003e result on reconnect or history replay (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/188\" data-hovercard-type=\"pull_request\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/188/hovercard\"\u003e#188\u003c/a\u003e, thanks @BillDin). Preset routing also got sharper: an explicitly named preset (e.g. \u003ccode\u003einvestment_committee\u003c/code\u003e, with or without underscores) now wins over keyword scoring, and the bare \u003ccode\u003eIV\u003c/code\u003e derivatives keyword no longer false-matches inside ordinary words like \"g\u003cstrong\u003eiv\u003c/strong\u003een\" (\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/189\" data-hovercard-type=\"pull_request\" data-hovercard-url=\"/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/189/hovercard\"\u003e#189\u003c/a\u003e, thanks @BillDin).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2026-06-06\u003c/strong\u003e ⚖️ \u003cstrong\u003eAlpha compare — head-to-head across CLI, Web UI, REST \u0026amp; agent\u003c/strong\u003e: A new \u003ccode\u003ealpha compare\u003c/code\u003e benches a hand-picked shortlist of Alpha Zoo alphas against each other on a universe and period, then ranks them by IC mean/std, IR, IC-positive ratio or sample count — each with its gap to the leader. Unlike a full-zoo bench it evaluates \u003cstrong\u003eonly the alphas you name\u003c/strong\u003e (a new \u003ccode\u003erun_bench(only=…)\u003c/code\u003e subset filter), so comparing three alphas no longer scores all 191 in their zoo. See \u003ccode\u003e.env.example\u003c/code\u003e for config.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTip:\u003c/strong\u003e All markets work without any API keys thanks to automatic fallback. yfinance (HK/US), OKX (crypto), mootdx (A-shares, TCP-direct, no IP throttle), and AKShare (A-shares, US, HK, futures, forex) are all free. This relies on the \u003ccode\u003ehost-gateway\u003c/code\u003e mapping in \u003ccode\u003eextra_hosts\u003c/code\u003e, which requires \u003cstrong\u003eDocker Engine ≥ 20.10 / Compose v2\u003c/strong\u003e (provided automatically on Docker Desktop).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYour data survives updates: persistent memory, the cross-session search index, user-created skills, shadow accounts, broker connector config, web sessions, backtest runs, swarm history, and uploads all live in named Docker volumes, so \u003ccode\u003egit pull \u0026amp;\u0026amp; docker compose up --build\u003c/code\u003e keeps them. class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="feat(factors): Alpha Zoo framework — registry, operators, safety gates

New module agent/src/factors/ providing the foundation for the Alpha
Zoo:

- base.py: 19 cross-sectional + time-series operators on wide
  pd.DataFrame panels (rank/scale/ts_*/delta/decay_linear/signed_power/
  safe_div + market-aware vwap). NaN propagates strictly; delta(d>=1)
  enforced at the operator layer; no negative shifts allowed.
- registry.py: AST-extracts __alpha_meta__ from each zoo .py module
  without importing it; pydantic AlphaMeta (extra="forbid",
  frozen=True). Lazy importlib.import_module on compute(); filesystem-
  loader fallback for plugin/test trees. Sanity gates reject +/-inf,
  NaN ratio > 95%, and shape mismatches.
- factor_analysis_core.py: IC/IR + layered backtest math extracted
  from agent/src/tools/factor_analysis_tool.py so it's reusable from
  CLI, bench tool, and API.
- bench_runner.py: per-alpha compute → IC vs forward return →
  alive/reversed/dead categorisation (mean IC > 0.02, pos_ratio >=
  0.55, |t-stat| > 2). Shared by CLI driver and API worker.

Multi-factor skill gains a panel-style ZooSignalEngine.from_zoo()
factory (cross-sectional standardisation + weighting + optional
top-N / bottom-N long-short conversion). The legacy per-symbol
example_signal_engine.py is left untouched. SKILL.md edits in
multi-factor and factor-research cross-reference the new zoo.

Safety floor:
- test_alpha_purity.py: AST allowlist scan of every zoo/**/*.py
  module. Allowed imports: pandas, numpy, scipy.*, src.factors.base,
  __future__, typing, math, dataclasses. Banned names: os/sys/
  subprocess/socket/urllib/requests/httpx/pathlib/Path/open/eval/exec/
  compile/__import__, plus dunder-access via getattr(_, "__*"),
  breakpoint, input, help, memoryview, globals, locals, vars, and
  the __class__/__bases__/__mro__/__globals__/__builtins__ chain.
  Module-level statements limited to docstring + imports + functions
  + ALPHA_ID/__alpha_meta__ assignments with literal RHS.
- test_lookahead.py: 300-row synthetic panel; corrupt rows >= 270;
  assert factor at probe row 260 unchanged within 1e-9.
- test_base.py + test_registry.py + conftest.py with opt-in
  pytest-socket integration that hard-fails outbound network during
  the factors test suite.
- tools/ci_grep_gates.sh: rejects yaml.load( without safe_load,
  any trademarked-name leak in shipped artifacts, and any per-stock-
  code data leak in wiki/**/*.{json,csv,html}.

Governance:

persist user agent state across container rebuilds

All user-level agent state lives under ~/.vibe-trading in the container
(persistent memory, sessions.db search index, user-created skills,
shadow accounts, hypothesis registry, broker connector config), but
docker-compose only mounted volumes for web sessions and backtest runs.
Every `docker compose up --build` therefore recreated the container and
silently wiped the user's memory store (#197). Swarm run history and
uploads were lost the same way.

- Mount vibe-home -> /home/vibe/.vibe-trading, plus vibe-swarm-runs and
  vibe-uploads.
- Pre-create /home/vibe/.vibe-trading owned by the service user in the
  Dockerfile so the named volume inherits writable permissions (a named
  volume mounted onto a missing path is created root-owned and the
  non-root user cannot write).
- README: document what persists across updates.

Verified end-to-end: memory written via PersistentMemory in one
container is intact in a fresh container on the same volume; the
counterfactual run without the volume reproduces the wipe.

Fixes #197." class="Link--secondary" href="/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/commit/1a356da369846d7f2385caa1acda06bb5273b195">fix(docker): persist user agent state across container New module agent/src/factors/ providing the foundation for the Alpha
Zoo:

- base.py: 19 cross-sectional + time-series operators on wide
  pd.DataFrame panels (rank/scale/ts_*/delta/decay_linear/signed_power/
  safe_div + market-aware vwap). NaN propagates strictly; delta(d>=1)

- registry.py: AST-extracts __alpha_meta__ from each zoo .py module
  without importing it; pydantic AlphaMeta (extra="forbid",
  frozen=True). Lazy importlib.import_module on compute(); filesystem-
  loader fallback for plugin/test trees. Sanity gates reject +/-inf,
  NaN ratio > 95%, and shape mismatches.
- factor_analysis_core.py: IC/IR + layered backtest math extracted
  from agent/src/tools/factor_analysis_tool.py so it's reusable from
  CLI, bench tool, and API.
- bench_runner.py: per-alpha compute → IC vs forward return →
  alive/reversed/dead categorisation (mean IC > 0.02, pos_ratio >=
  0.55, |t-stat| > 2). Shared by CLI driver and API worker.

Multi-factor skill gains a panel-style ZooSignalEngine.from_zoo()
factory (cross-sectional standardisation + weighting + optional
top-N / bottom-N long-short conversion). The legacy per-symbol
example_signal_engine.py is left untouched. SKILL.md edits in
multi-factor and factor-research cross-reference the new zoo.

Safety floor:
- test_alpha_purity.py: AST allowlist scan of every zoo/**/*.py
  module. Allowed imports: pandas, numpy, scipy.*, src.factors.base,
  __future__, typing, math, dataclasses. Banned names: os/sys/
  subprocess/socket/urllib/requests/httpx/pathlib/Path/open/eval/exec/
  compile/__import__, plus dunder-access via getattr(_, "__*"),
  breakpoint, input, help, memoryview, globals, locals, vars, and
  the __class__/__bases__/__mro__/__globals__/__builtins__ chain.
  Module-level statements limited to docstring + imports + functions
  + ALPHA_ID/__alpha_meta__ assignments with literal RHS.
- test_lookahead.py: 300-row synthetic panel; corrupt rows >= 270;
  assert factor at probe row 260 unchanged within 1e-9.
- test_base.py + test_registry.py + conftest.py with opt-in
  pytest-socket integration that hard-fails outbound network during
  the factors test suite.
- tools/ci_grep_gates.sh: rejects yaml.load( without safe_load,
  any trademarked-name leak in shipped artifacts, and any per-stock-
  code data leak in wiki/**/*.{json,csv,html}.

Governance:
- CONTRIBUTING.md with the Developer Certificate of Origin trailer
  for community PRs and the alpha PR reviewer checklist.

title="fix(docker): persist user agent state across container rebuilds

All user-level agent state lives under ~/.vibe-trading in the container
(persistent memory, sessions.db search index, user-created skills,
shadow accounts, hypothesis registry, broker connector config), but
docker-compose only mounted volumes for web sessions and backtest runs.
Every `docker compose up --build` therefore recreated the container and
silently wiped the user's memory store (#197). Swarm run history and
uploads were lost the same way.

- Mount vibe-home -> /home/vibe/.vibe-trading, plus vibe-swarm-runs and
  vibe-uploads.
- Pre-create /home/vibe/.vibe-trading owned by the service user in the
  Dockerfile so the named volume inherits writable permissions (a named
  volume mounted onto a missing path is created root-owned and the
  non-root user cannot write).
- README: document what persists across updates.

Verified end-to-end: memory written via PersistentMemory in one
container is intact in a fresh container on the same volume; the
counterfactual run without the volume reproduces the wipe.

Fixes #197." class="Link--secondary" href="/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/commit/1a356da369846d7f2385caa1acda06bb5273b195">fix(docker): persist user agent state across container <li><strong>2026-06-11</strong> 🐝 <strong>Swarm workers now pull market data through the loader layer</strong>: An investment-committee run on NVDA exposed a chain of gaps — workers wrote ad-hoc yfinance scripts, trusted a malformed latest bar (volume present, OHLC empty), leaked <code>NaN</code> into non-strict JSON, and a context-free continuation prompt re-routed to the wrong preset (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/198" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/198/hovercard" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">#198</a>, thanks @BillDin for an exceptional diagnosis plus both fixes). Swarm workers now get a local <code>get_market_data</code> tool backed by the same normalized loader registry as MCP — strict JSON, non-finite floats serialize as <code>null</code> — wired into <strong>every market-data preset</strong> (21 workers across 13 presets) with a prompt policy that steers OHLCV work tool-first (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/199" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/199/hovercard" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">#199</a>); <code>run_swarm</code> takes an explicit <code>preset_name</code> and refuses ambiguous continuation fragments instead of silently falling back to <code>equity_research_team</code> (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/200" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/200/hovercard" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">#200</a>). Grounding got smarter too: a bare US ticker like <code>NVDA</code> in a swarm prompt is promoted to <code>NVDA.US</code> (stopword-guarded), so workers start from authoritative pre-fetched prices. The tool joins the main agent registry as well — <strong>48 tools</strong> now. Also: <strong>your Docker data now survives updates</strong> — persistent memory, the session search index, user-created skills, shadow accounts and broker config live in named volumes, so <code>docker compose up --build</code> no longer wipes them (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/197" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/197/hovercard" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">#197</a>, thanks @FlyerJ).</li>
<li><strong>2026-06-10</strong> 🐳 <strong>Docker reaches a host-side Ollama out of the box</strong>: Inside the container <code>localhost</code> is the container itself, so the shipped <code>OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434</code> failed the LLM preflight for every Dockerized Ollama setup. <code>docker-compose.yml</code> now defaults to <code>http://host.docker.internal:11434</code> (export <code>OLLAMA_BASE_URL</code> to point elsewhere) and adds the <code>host-gateway</code> <code>extra_hosts</code> mapping so the same file works on Linux as well as Docker Desktop (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/196" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/pull/196/hovercard" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">#196</a>, thanks @ShahNewazKhan).</li>
<li><strong>2026-06-09</strong> 🔑 <strong>Clearer error when the Web UI is opened from another machine</strong>: Reaching the chat from a non-loopback client (another machine, a VM host, a phone on your LAN) without <code>API_AUTH_KEY</code> set returned <code>403</code> on every sensitive endpoint — sending a message, listing sessions, live status — but the chat only showed a generic "Failed to send message, please retry." The send path now surfaces the real reason — <em>"Remote API access requires an API key. Add it in Settings, or run the backend on localhost for local-only use."</em> — and the README's web-UI setup spells out the localhost-vs-LAN rule plus the three fixes (browse via <code>localhost</code> on the same machine; set <code>API_AUTH_KEY</code> and enter it once in Settings; or <code>VIBE_TRADING_TRUST_DOCKER_LOOPBACK=1</code> for Docker Desktop's host gateway) (<a href="https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/191" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading/issues/191/hovercard" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">#191</a>, thanks @mafia23).</li>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">💡 What Is Vibe-Trading?</h2><a id="user-content--what-is-vibe-trading" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 💡 What Is Vibe-Trading?" href="#-what-is-vibe-trading"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Vibe-Trading is an open-source research workspace for turning finance questions into runnable analysis. It connects natural-language prompts to market-data loaders, strategy generation, backtest engines, reports, exports, and persistent research memory.</p>
<p dir="auto">It is designed for research, simulation, and backtesting — and, when you choose, autonomous trading through a broker you authorize yourself (e.g. Robinhood Agentic Trading). It holds no funds and never trades outside the limits you set, and you can halt it instantly.</p>

<code>agent/backtest/loaders/registry.py</code>.</p>

</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><em>(Optional)</em> slot it into a market's <code>FALLBACK_CHAINS</code> in <code>registry.py</code> so

</li>

</li>

loader layer is point-in-time historical bars only. Live market data flows
through the broker connectors instead: <code>okx</code> / <code>binance</code> / <code>ccxt</code> for crypto,
<code>futu</code> / <code>tiger</code> for equities.</p>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>An <strong>LLM API key</strong> from any supported provider — or run locally with <strong>Ollama</strong> (no key needed)</li>

<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Supported LLM providers:</strong> OpenRouter, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, Groq, DashScope/Qwen, Zhipu, Moonshot/Kimi, MiniMax, Xiaomi MIMO, Z.ai, Ollama (local). See <code>.env.example</code> for config.</p>
</blockquote>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Tip:</strong> All markets work without any API keys thanks to automatic fallback. yfinance (HK/US), OKX (crypto), mootdx (A-shares, TCP-direct, no IP throttle), and AKShare (A-shares, US, HK, futures, forex) are all free. Tushare token is optional — mootdx is the preferred no-token A-share fallback, with AKShare as a broader backup.</p>
</blockquote>

<p dir="auto">Open <code>http://localhost:8899</code>. Backend + frontend in one container.</p>
<p dir="auto">Docker publishes the backend on <code>127.0.0.1:8899</code> by default and runs the app as a non-root container user. If you intentionally expose the API beyond your own machine, set a strong <code>API_AUTH_KEY</code> and send <code>Authorization: Bearer <key></code> from clients.</p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-note" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-info mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 8a8 8 0 1 1 16 0A8 8 0 0 1 0 8Zm8-6.5a6.5 6.5 0 1 0 0 13 6.5 6.5 0 0 0 0-13ZM6.5 7.75A.75.75 0 0 1 7.25 7h1a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.75h.25a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5h-2a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.5h.25v-2h-.25a.75.75 0 0 1-.75-.75ZM8 6a1 1 0 1 1 0-2 1 1 0 0 1 0 2Z"></path></svg>Note</p><p dir="auto"><strong>Using Ollama with Docker:</strong> the container reaches a host-side Ollama via <code>host.docker.internal</code>, not <code>localhost</code> (inside the container <code>localhost</code> is the container itself). <code>docker-compose.yml</code> defaults <code>OLLAMA_BASE_URL</code> to <code>http://host.docker.internal:11434</code>; export <code>OLLAMA_BASE_URL</code> (or set it in a top-level <code>.env</code>) to point elsewhere. This relies on the <code>host-gateway</code> mapping in <code>extra_hosts</code>, which requires <strong>Docker Engine ≥ 20.10 / Compose v2</strong> (provided automatically on Docker Desktop).</p>
</div>
<p dir="auto">Your data survives updates: persistent memory, the cross-session search index, user-created skills, shadow accounts, broker connector config, web sessions, backtest runs, swarm history, and uploads all live in named Docker volumes, so <code>git pull && docker compose up --build</code> keeps them. They are deleted only by <code>docker compose down -v</code>.</p>

<p dir="auto">Copy <code>agent/.env.example</code> to <code>agent/.env</code> and uncomment the provider block you want. Each provider needs 3-4 variables:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Variable</th>
<th align="center">Required</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>LANGCHAIN_PROVIDER</code></td>
<td align="center">Yes</td>
<td>Provider name (<code>openrouter</code>, <code>deepseek</code>, <code>groq</code>, <code>ollama</code>, etc.)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code><PROVIDER>_API_KEY</code></td>
<td align="center">Yes*</td>
<td>API key (<code>OPENROUTER_API_KEY</code>, <code>DEEPSEEK_API_KEY</code>, etc.)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code><PROVIDER>_BASE_URL</code></td>
<td align="center">Yes</td>
<td>API endpoint URL</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>LANGCHAIN_MODEL_NAME</code></td>
<td align="center">Yes</td>
<td>Model name (e.g. <code>deepseek-v4-pro</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>TUSHARE_TOKEN</code></td>
<td align="center">No</td>
<td>Tushare Pro token for A-share data (falls back to AKShare)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>TIMEOUT_SECONDS</code></td>
<td align="center">No</td>
<td>LLM call timeout, default 120s</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>API_AUTH_KEY</code></td>
<td align="center">Recommended for network deployments</td>
<td>Bearer token required when the API is reachable from non-local clients</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>VIBE_TRADING_ENABLE_SHELL_TOOLS</code></td>
<td align="center">No</td>
<td>Explicit opt-in for shell-capable tools in remote API/MCP-SSE style deployments</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>VIBE_TRADING_ALLOWED_FILE_ROOTS</code></td>
<td align="center">No</td>
<td>Extra comma-separated roots for document and broker-journal imports</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>VIBE_TRADING_ALLOWED_RUN_ROOTS</code></td>
<td align="center">No</td>
<td>Extra comma-separated roots for generated-code run directories</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto"><sub>* Ollama does not require an API key. OpenAI Codex uses ChatGPT OAuth and stores tokens via <code>oauth-cli-kit</code>, not in <code>agent/.env</code>.</sub></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Free data (no key needed):</strong> A-shares via AKShare, HK/US equities via yfinance, crypto via OKX, 100+ crypto exchanges via CCXT. The system automatically selects the best available source for each market.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">🎯 Recommended Models</h3><a id="user-content--recommended-models" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 🎯 Recommended Models" href="#-recommended-models"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Vibe-Trading is a tool-heavy agent — skills, backtests, memory, and swarms all flow through tool calls. Model choice directly decides whether the agent <em>uses</em> its tools or fabricates answers from training data.</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Tier</th>
<th>Examples</th>
<th>When to use</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Best</strong></td>
<td><code>anthropic/claude-opus-4.7</code>, <code>anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6</code>, <code>openai/gpt-5.5-pro</code>, <code>google/gemini-3.5-flash</code></td>
<td>Complex swarms (3+ agents), long research sessions, paper-grade analysis</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Sweet spot</strong> (default)</td>
<td><code>deepseek-v4-pro</code>, <code>deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro</code>, <code>x-ai/grok-4.20</code>, <code>z-ai/glm-5.1</code>, <code>moonshotai/kimi-k2.6</code>, <code>qwen/qwen3-max-thinking</code></td>
<td>Daily driver — reliable tool-calling at ~1/10 the cost</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Avoid for agent use</strong></td>
<td><code>*-nano</code>, <code>*-flash-lite</code>, <code>*-coder-next</code>, small / distilled variants</td>
<td>Tool-calling is unreliable — the agent will appear to "answer from memory" instead of loading skills or running backtests</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">The default <code>agent/.env.example</code> ships with DeepSeek official API + <code>deepseek-v4-pro</code>; OpenRouter users can use <code>deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro</code>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Security defaults</h3><a id="user-content-security-defaults" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Security defaults" href="#security-defaults"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">For localhost development, <code>vibe-trading serve</code> keeps the browser workflow simple. For any non-local client, sensitive API endpoints require <code>API_AUTH_KEY</code>; use <code>Authorization: Bearer <key></code> for JSON/upload requests. Browser EventSource streams are handled by the Web UI after you enter the same key once in Settings.</p>
<p dir="auto">Shell-capable tools are available to local CLI and trusted localhost workflows, but are not exposed to remote API sessions unless you explicitly set <code>VIBE_TRADING_ENABLE_SHELL_TOOLS=1</code>. Document and journal readers are limited to upload/import roots by default; place files under <code>agent/uploads</code>, <code>agent/runs</code>, <code>./uploads</code>, <code>./data</code>, <code>~/.vibe-trading/uploads</code>, or <code>~/.vibe-trading/imports</code>, or add a dedicated directory through <code>VIBE_TRADING_ALLOWED_FILE_ROOTS</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Web UI Settings</h3><a id="user-content-web-ui-settings" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Web UI Settings" href="#web-ui-settings"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The Web UI Settings page lets local users update the LLM provider/model, base URL, generation parameters, reasoning effort, and optional market data credentials such as the Tushare token. Settings are persisted to <code>agent/.env</code>; provider defaults are loaded from <code>agent/src/providers/llm_providers.json</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Settings reads are side-effect free: <code>GET /settings/llm</code> and <code>GET /settings/data-sources</code> never create <code>agent/.env</code>, and they only return project-relative paths. Settings reads and writes can expose credential state or update credentials/runtime environment, so they require <code>API_AUTH_KEY</code> when configured. If <code>API_AUTH_KEY</code> is unset for dev mode, settings access is accepted only from loopback clients.</p>

<p dir="auto"><code>run_swarm</code> workers can call operator-approved tools from external MCP servers. Configure the server-side allowlist in <code>VIBE_TRADING_SWARM_AGENT_CONFIG</code>, <code>~/.vibe-trading/swarm-agent.json</code>, or the fallback <code>~/.vibe-trading/agent.json</code>; then list remote tools in a swarm preset using the local MCP wrapper name, such as <code>mcp_internal_kb_search</code>. <p dir="auto">Vibe-Trading can connect directly to Interactive Brokers' official remote MCP
endpoint in read-only mode. Add this to <code>~/.vibe-trading/agent.json</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"mcpServers"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"ibkr"</span>: {
      <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>streamableHttp<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"url"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/mcp<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"auth"</span>: {
        <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>oauth<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"scopes"</span>: [<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>mcp.read<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>],
        <span class="pl-ent">"clientName"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Vibe-Trading<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"cacheDir"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>~/.vibe-trading/live/ibkr/oauth<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
      },
      <span class="pl-ent">"enabledTools"</span>: [<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>*<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>]
    }
  }
}</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto">The wildcard is accepted only for IBKR's <code>mcp.read</code> probe. Authorizing this
profile confirms access to IBKR's official read scope; generic <code>trading_account</code>
and <code>trading_positions</code> calls stay disabled until IBKR publishes stable read
tool names that Vibe-Trading can map safely. A config that adds <code>mcp.write</code> must
pin an explicit tool allowlist and still passes through the live order guard.</p>
<p dir="auto">If IBKR issues a pre-registered OAuth client, add <code>clientId</code> and <code>clientSecret</code>
inside <code>auth</code>.</p>

TWS or IB Gateway session. Credentials stay inside IBKR's desktop app; Vibe-
Trading only connects to <code>127.0.0.1</code> and exposes it as a connector profile.</p>

<p dir="auto">The agent exposes connector-scoped tools named <code>trading_connections</code>,
<code>trading_select_connection</code>, <code>trading_check</code>, <code>trading_account</code>,
<code>trading_positions</code>, <code>trading_orders</code>, <code>trading_quote</code>, and <code>trading_history</code>.
Live-broker raw MCP tools are not registered directly as <code>mcp_<broker>_*</code>.
No IBKR order-placement tool is registered.</p>

<p dir="auto">Config file location: <code>~/.vibe-trading/agent.json</code> (JSON or YAML).</p>
<p dir="auto">For URL-based transports, <code>type</code> is required. The agent no longer guesses between SSE and streamable HTTP from the URL suffix.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Per-session overrides (API)</h3><a id="user-content-per-session-overrides-api" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Per-session overrides (API)" href="#per-session-overrides-api"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Tool naming</h3><a id="user-content-tool-naming" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Tool naming" href="#tool-naming"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Ordinary remote tools are exposed with stable names: <code>mcp_<server>_<tool></code>.
Live-broker MCP servers stay behind the <code>trading_*</code> connector surface.</p>
<p dir="auto">If two server names produce the same ASCII-safe local prefix (e.g. <code>foo-bar</code> and <code>foo_bar</code> both become <code>foo_bar</code>), a deterministic hash suffix is appended at the server-segment level so names remain unique. The operator receives a warning:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto"><pre class="notranslate"><code>WARNING: Configured MCP server 'foo-bar' collides with another server after local name
normalization. Using local tool prefix 'mcp_foo_bar_<hash>_<tool>' to keep generated
tool names unique. Rename the server in agent config if you want a different prefix.
</code></pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Limit</th>
<th>Detail</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Transport</td>
<td>stdio, SSE, and streamable HTTP</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Execution</td>
<td>serial only — MCP tools never enter the parallel readonly path</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Surfaces</td>
<td>tools only (resources and prompts excluded in v1)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Hot reload</td>
<td>not supported — restart the process to pick up config changes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Swarm path</td>
<td>MCP tools are not available inside Swarm worker registries in v1</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
